### 2026-10-20 – # Starting Maestro Mini

**2h**

# Starting Maestro Mini
This device is going to be a tool/loop synth. It will have different utility options, which will be rotated by a Control push button. To be fair, I am still in the process of finalizing the design, but I have still made some progress so far. Again, whatever I have here for the design or schematics might change in the future.
## What I did
- Researched what components I would need. Since I plan to use the XIAO ESP32 C3 once again for this project, and I need around 10 pushbuttons, I will use MCP23017, a 16bit I/O port expander.
- As of now, I created the repository for this week's project and started on the schematic using KiCad. For now, I have the MCP23017 and the 10 pushbuttons in place and connected with the necessary resistors.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/787f249301917e91867f599039a947ef16f3aa324e5b4ee8e53168b322e3006d.png)

## What I will do next
- Add and connect the ESP32, the OLED screen, and other components.

### 2026-10-25 – # Finishing Everything!!

**9h**

# Finishing Everything!!
I had so much to do today...
## What I did
- I created the PCB outline. Since I will probably not be able to design an enclosure for it due to time constraints, I decided to go with a round corner rectangle. I also did some rearranging of the components so they don't look so disorganized.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/8f0b81df40ebb2ded6535f043afc9d4ff42a7057f0bc30be1b57c9f60efd3cc1.png)
- Once the outline was done, I had to start wiring. Because of my 10 buttons and all the other components, it meant that there were a lot of components I had to connect. To keep it more organized and easier for me, I decided to connect the buttons through the back of the board, and the rest through the front. I did need to add some vias through the back so that everything would connect where it needed to. I also added ground pours to both sides to reduce the amount of wiring I had to do.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/747b247005730b0a12ce42efec2f355412a732c0289cfa5b4937080448761780.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/ce225fea62d69dd22e4cb6a8f86b9877737ba054f860e046340d4d9a0bca2bea.png)
- I started to look at the rechargable battery I would use, and I found one, but I realized that the battery will absolutely not have any space in my current layout of the board! To not move around the components much, I simply decided to flip the pins to the backside of the board, in which it will have plenty of space.

![Untitled drawing 21](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/df845c0685b4f3576e3937869493db96f3121695bd1193f8bbaf464105632bca.png)

![Untitled drawing 20](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/9ba6b669555d9c0188424d214970e484a3b364290cf9a948f8988e2f099ae259.png)

- I finalized the audio jack component. Before, I simply had it as three pins, but instead I went for a 4 pins audio jack, a PJ-320. I had to change the schematics to match this 4 pin audiojack, and also the footprint. There was only a surface mount footprint, so I guess I will surface mount that component.

![Untitled drawing 23](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/3488bef108821a1aa94df65c7a47e803711b0c0114c1cf0ade2b78ce9bdb0de9.png)
- I added the 3D models to each  component's footprint. I reused some from the Care Package from the week 1 Astrobie guide, but I also found ones on my own, such as for the audio jack and the switch. The closest I could find to the Adafruit PAM8302 was simply a rounded corners prism without any details of it, but that is (hopefully) to scale.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/b13d73e5969cdffde8dcbfac0ace4799a1ec61132c1294c95eb2e4ecbb4a35ac.png)

- I ran into various errors in the DRC for the PCB. For example, there was a problem with the footprint design in which the courtyard rectangle was not properly closed off. The DRC also detected a short circuit where a trace was going through a ground pad. I had to reroute the trace so that it would not come in contact anymore. Various ground pads were in an isolated copper pool. Finally, I got "Zone min spoke count 2; actual 1" errors for some of the ground pads, who did not get the required 2 copper bridges because there were traces too close to them. These were all fixed, and now there are no errors when running the DRC. There are no errors in the ERC either (for the schematics).

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 132736](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/ed7673fd80bfb37a84d98956a05ca70c6296eb8bf815476dd9f5b7513ce2929d.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 134046](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/902959bf90ea9a3f68bf898fda9da696a672924c9826db4f691a5c593e5efd36.png)

## Drastic Changes
I wanted to see how much the cost of everything would turn out. By looking for all the components in AliExpress, it was a few dollars under $65. That is without the PCB, so for sure I would go over that cap for a tier 2 project. I decided that I am complicating myself too much. The project was honestly too ambitious to finish it in such little time :(

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 162811](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/7e6389b2a23d3120b6c69b872c98641c817e70f324901782ba29dadc944ad8da.png)

My solution is removing two aspects that are not absolutely necessary to the project: the rechargable battery and the audiojack. So I removed them! Since I removed the battery, meaning that the device will only work when it is wired to the computer, I don't need the on/off switch anymore.

![Untitled drawing 24](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/63f6966ccd164d612dad87f9ae07db2d72e22c52875886c19a1744e09ae0cce4.png)

I decided to ultimately go with Alibaba because the prices were cheaper. I completed the final BOM. I've already got the 1k resistor, so I didn't include it.

## Coding
- Installed the Adafruit MCP23017 library in the Arduino IDE.
- Coded!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/e74ad44e423666653ce9cdd42e25fe7ea3b6c7d26cba4fd199048bcb54f4ea01.png)

So that is it, done on time! I really hope the project gets accepted and that, if it does, everything works during the build week...
